_note: v2 hook overrides for la montagne (B26_montagne). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting can show them; these replace only hooks whose setting does not fit the ski slopes or that differ from what is painted (several source hooks used a goat; one goat is kept for la montagne, the others became different animals or people so each picture is distinct).

fr_cote_noun_2.hook: A COAT ("KOHT") dries on a rope between two posts at the edge of the ski SLOPE, flapping in the mountain breeze. (La côte is a coast, and also a hillside slope.)
fr_cote_noun_2.why: Source hook is set on the sea coast; this room is the mountain, so the painting uses the 'slope' sense with the same coat.

fr_rocher_noun.hook: "Row, Shay!" ("roh-SHAY"): a girl called Shay ROWS her little wooden boat through the deep snow, right past a big ROCK.
fr_rocher_noun.why: Owner's review 2026-10-25: le rocher is a person rowing a boat through the snow (row-Shay); replaces the seal.

fr_descente_noun.hook: Like English 'descent', said day-SAHNT: a skier makes his DESCENT straight down the slope toward a steaming apple pie sitting on the snow, following its SCENT.
fr_descente_noun.why: Owner's review 2026-10-25: the apple pie now sits right on the skier's way down (the old pie by the tent was removed).

fr_saut_noun.hook: A frog takes a big JUMP off the ski jump: "so" high!
fr_saut_noun.why: Source has the frog jumping over a puddle; on the slopes it flies off a ski jump.

fr_monture_noun.hook: A knight sits proudly on his MOUNT ("mohn-TEWR"), a white horse, at the foot of the crag.
fr_monture_noun.why: Painting shows the knight already in the saddle rather than climbing on.

fr_ascension_noun.hook: Like English 'ascent', said ah-sahn-SYOHN: the ASCENT of the mountain: a little boy climbs with a tiny backpack and plants a flag.
fr_ascension_noun.why: Source uses a goat (the goat is la montagne); the little bear that replaced it broke Lesson 2, so a boy climbs now (repainted).

fr_cime_noun.hook: A giant zip seam ("SEEM") runs up to the very PEAK of the snowy mountain, like the top of a sleeping bag.
fr_cime_noun.why: Painting shows the zip on the peak without the goat (the goat is la montagne).

fr_val_noun.hook: Like English 'vale', said VAHL: Val, a girl in green, skips through a little green VALE between the snowy slopes.
fr_val_noun.why: Source makes Val a goat; Val is painted as a girl to keep the goats distinct.

fr_foulee_noun.hook: A court jester takes one giant STRIDE over an icy puddle, bells jingling: "A fool, eh?" ("foo-LAY").
fr_foulee_noun.why: The king is not painted; the jester's stride is.

fr_sierra_noun.hook: Like English 'sierra', said syeh-RAH: a giant SAW stands beside a SIERRA of jagged peaks whose points match its teeth.
fr_sierra_noun.why: Painting shows the saw beside the peaks; no goat (the goat is la montagne).

fr_alpiniste_noun.hook: Like English 'mountaineer', said ahl-pih-NEEST: a MOUNTAINEER in a red helmet clips her rope to the peak, grinning.
fr_alpiniste_noun.why: Source makes the mountaineer a goat; the painting shows a woman mountaineer.

fr_talus_noun.hook: Like English 'talus', said tah-LEW, a 'tall loo': a comically TALL LOO rides a sled down the steep snowy EMBANKMENT.
fr_talus_noun.why: Owner's review 2026-10-25: le talus = a tall loo riding down the slope (owner-approved, kept clean and cartoonish).

fr_grotte_noun.hook: Like English 'grotto', said GROT: a skier ducks into a mountain CAVE and finds a grumpy old caretaker sweeping out the GROT.
fr_grotte_noun.why: Source has a polar bear sweeping. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook, so a person does the action now (repainted).

fr_sommet_noun.hook: Like English 'summit', said soh-MEH: a girl hiker in a woolly hat finally reaches the snowy SUMMIT, glances at the view and shrugs, "so... meh."
fr_sommet_noun.why: Source has a llama in a woolly hat. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook, so a person does the action now (repainted).

fr_ski_noun.hook: Like English 'ski', said SKEE: a little boy on SKIS whizzes down the slope, arms out like a jumbo jet.
fr_ski_noun.why: Source has a penguin skiing. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook, so a person does the action now (repainted).

fr_rampe_noun.hook: Like English 'ramp', said RAHNP: a snowboarding girl zooms up a RAMP and does a triple flip.
fr_rampe_noun.why: Source has a snowboarding penguin. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook, so a person does the action now (repainted).

fr_escalade_noun.hook: Like English 'escalade', said ehs-kah-LAHD: a girl in a helmet tackles the ROCK CLIMB, SCALING the cliff on a rope.
fr_escalade_noun.why: Source has a goat climbing with a rope. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook, so a person does the action now (repainted).

fr_caverne_noun.hook: Like English 'cavern', said kah-VEHRN: a ski-slope CAVERN full of icicles, and a big brown bear fast asleep inside.
fr_caverne_noun.why: Source bear wore a woolly hat; Lesson 2: it is now a plain sleeping bear (repainted).

fr_traction_noun.hook: Like English 'traction', said trahk-SYOHN: a PULL-UP on the ski lift bar, done by a red-faced boy straining with all his might.
fr_traction_noun.why: Source has a muscly marmot. Lesson 2: no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal IS the hook, so a person does the action now (repainted).

fr_chamois_noun.hook: Like English 'chamois', said shah-MWAH: a CHAMOIS on a rocky ledge beside the glacier puckers up and blows a big kiss: MWAH!
fr_chamois_noun.why: 'shah-MWAH' = kiss sound; real chamois on a ledge above the ice

fr_echo_noun.hook: Like English 'echo', said ay-KOH: a boy on the ski slope cups his hands and shouts at the mountain, and the ECHO comes bouncing back to him.
fr_echo_noun.why: Paint-back: plan-only since p20 (from plage/plage); painted into montagne/montagne (R_mountain_01, its planned room).

fr_hauteur_noun.hook: A climber on a high tower ("oh-TUHR") measures the HEIGHT with a long ribbon.
fr_hauteur_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (o-TUR -> oh-TUHR).
